tasks.short: Answer public questions about published material, editorial choices and corrections.

steps.what: Read incoming questions, log them and identify the responsible editor.
Find the publication, supporting sources and relevant editorial policy.

loop.input: Question record and permission-filtered publication archive, source packs and editorial policies.
loop.output: Relevant passages with document links and an explicit missing-evidence flag.
loop.check: Validate document access, passage existence and policy version; editor checks relevance.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one refinement per question; unresolved questions return to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search misses questions phrased differently from the underlying material.

steps.what: Draft a response explaining the answer and any uncertainty.

loop.input: Question record, checked answer evidence and approved response templates.
loop.output: Response draft with internal citations and unresolved points.
loop.check: Require support for factual statements; prohibit invented quotations and commitments; editor checks meaning and tone.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unsupported answers remain drafts for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover acknowledgements, but substantive questions need contextual explanation.

steps.what: Approve and send straightforward answers.
Discuss disputed coverage, sensitive corrections or unresolved concerns with the questioner.

tasks.design: Configure a question queue in the {HELPDESK}, connected to the {EMAIL}, and retrieve permission-filtered evidence from the {CMS} and {DOCS}. A bounded loop prepares cited responses; the editor approves each substantive outgoing answer, while sensitive conversations stay with the editor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers require scattered sources, editorial context and a suitable tone. Mailbox rules alone cannot supply these.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queues handle routing, while retrieval and bounded drafting can prepare a reviewable answer with source links.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, correction commitments and trust require judgement. Correspondence can contain personal data despite concerning public material.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising the concern behind a question and deciding when an explanation, correction or personal conversation is needed.

ambition.what: A monthly reader-question digest that explains recurring editorial choices.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time finding material and typing repeated explanations, and more time resolving disputed coverage. With delegated authority, the editor can commission a clarification article from recurring questions.

reach.task: Prepare answers to recurring public concerns.
reach.learn: Escalation criteria, audience expectations and the difference between editorial explanation and organisational commitments.

evidence.claim: An archive chatbot trial supports retrieval feasibility, but does not establish reliable autonomous public replies.
The reported study of news answers supports retaining evidence checks before public responses.
Queue routing, approved templates and approval-triggered sending are standard configuration patterns.
GDPR applies to personal correspondence; marketing work should not assume a journalistic exemption.

assumptions: Questions usually arrive through a shared mailbox; sensitive cases sometimes move to a call.
The final conversation step applies only to escalations; its share is averaged across the question workload.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Consent and access estimates include privacy review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Question volume, repeated topics and current response times.
Archive completeness, source permissions and retention requirements.
Who can approve corrections and organisational commitments.
Whether the editor may commission clarification articles.
research_questions: Which question categories can use approved answers without contextual rewriting?
How often does retrieval omit evidence that changes the response?
Which concerns require a conversation rather than a written answer?
new_work: Review cited drafts and handle missing or conflicting evidence.
Maintain approved responses, routing rules and escalation criteria.
Keep archive permissions and retention controls aligned across connected systems.
Inspect recurring questions before preparing the reader-question digest.

tasks.short: Plan publication contents around audience needs, editorial policy, style and production requirements.

steps.what: Read the editorial policy, style guide and publication requirements.
Gather proposed articles, campaign dates and production capacity into the planning board.
Choose the audience priorities, subjects and balance of the publication.
Draft the contents, section order, article briefs and space allocations.

loop.input: Editor-selected priorities, eligible proposals and structured space, date and format constraints.
loop.output: Content plan with ordered sections, article briefs and constraint warnings.
loop.check: Code checks capacity, mandatory sections, dates and duplicate items; editor reviews coherence and briefs.
loop.stop: Generate one plan and one revision; unresolved conflicts return to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scheduling is deterministic, but turning varied proposals into coherent briefs requires language drafting.

steps.what: Agree the content plan and resolve competing stakeholder priorities.
Record assignments, deadlines and production slots from the approved plan.

tasks.design: Store versioned planning constraints in the {DOCS} and combine proposals, dates and capacity from the {CMS}, {CALENDAR} and {PROJECT}. Deterministic checks validate a bounded loop's draft content plan; approval then creates briefs and production assignments in the {PROJECT} and {CMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were prose, proposals differed in format, and production constraints lived in separate places. Planning still depended on editorial choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and structured constraint templates reduce assembly work. A bounded drafting loop can turn selected priorities into a consistent plan.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what matters, balancing stakeholder pressure and judging audience fatigue remain difficult. Capacity records can be stale.
tasks.human_edge: Setting a coherent editorial direction and defending audience needs when stakeholders compete for space.

ambition.what: A weekly content-mix review using production capacity and audience gaps.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends more of the week choosing coverage and improving briefs. With explicit delegation, the editor can move content within agreed production limits between formal planning meetings.

reach.task: Balance publication priorities against campaign objectives and available capacity.
reach.learn: Campaign dependencies, capacity planning and how to assess audience value beyond publication volume.

reach.task: Check whether planned sections fit the publication format.
reach.learn: Space budgets, layout constraints and production lead times.

evidence.claim: Acrolinx supports repeatable house-style checks; this does not establish automated editorial planning.
Structured constraints, capacity checks and approval-triggered assignments can use deterministic code and configuration.
The writing experiment supports assisted drafting feasibility, but provides no task-specific planning savings estimate.

assumptions: The publication is a corporate magazine, newsletter or comparable marketing publication.
Current policies can be converted into structured constraints with links to their original wording.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Consent and access includes data-owner approval and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Publication formats, cadence, mandatory sections and approval authority.
Whether production capacity and proposal status are recorded reliably.
Available integration access and ownership of planning constraints.
Whether the editor can move content between approved production slots.
research_questions: Which planning constraints are mandatory and which permit editorial exceptions?
Does generated planning reduce revision work or merely move it into review?
Which audience gaps can be measured without treating engagement as the sole objective?
new_work: Maintain structured constraints and check them against policy changes.
Resolve capacity conflicts and stale proposal records.
Review generated briefs and constraint warnings.
Maintain integrations and record why approved plans depart from recommendations.

tasks.short: Evaluate submissions, edit their content and style, and agree revisions with authors.

steps.what: Receive the manuscript and establish the current version and brief.
Read the manuscript and evaluate its argument, relevance and publication suitability.
Mark spelling, grammar, terminology and explicit house-style issues.
Revise structure and wording, adding comments where author clarification is needed.

loop.input: Manuscript, editor's assessment, source pack and approved style rules.
loop.output: Tracked revisions and author questions, with source links for factual changes.
loop.check: Protect quotations, names and numbers; run style checks; editor checks meaning and unsupported additions.
loop.stop: One revision pass and one repair per section; unresolved meaning returns as an author question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules detect surface issues but cannot draft context-sensitive structural changes.

steps.what: Discuss substantial changes and agree the intended meaning with the author.
Compare the author's revision against agreed changes and resolve remaining marks.
Accept the manuscript or require further revision before production.

tasks.design: Configure submission records, version comparison and rule-based copyediting in the {DOCS}, linked to the {CMS}. A bounded loop proposes tracked structural revisions from the editor's assessment; the editor reviews these before author discussion and explicitly approves the manuscript for production.
tasks.previous_blocker: Version handling and style checking were fragmented, while substantive editing depended on meaning and author intent.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing comparison and style tools cover routine work. Bounded drafting can now produce inspectable revisions tied to an editor's instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Preserving voice, detecting misleading omissions and resolving disagreement remain demanding. Source packs may not substantiate the manuscript.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding what the author means, improving the argument and deciding which changes justify challenging the author.

ambition.what: A supported contribution route for first-time subject-matter authors.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends more time on arguments, author development and difficult acceptance decisions. Acceptance authority remains unchanged; expanding the contributor pool requires an agreed editorial remit.

reach.task: Help subject-matter authors explain complex material accurately.
reach.learn: Task-based explanation, technical source validation and terminology management.

reach.task: Maintain consistent copyediting standards across recurring publications.
reach.learn: Rule exceptions, proof marks and the distinction between copyediting and final proof approval.

evidence.claim: LanguageTool provides spelling, grammar, punctuation and style checks.
Acrolinx supports repeatable style-guide scoring and quality gates.
The Roche case reports fewer translation edits; it supports style-control value, not a forecast for this editing workflow.
The documented invented-quotation failure supports protecting quotations and checking factual changes against sources.
GDPR, confidentiality and content rights need assessment before manuscript processing; marketing has no automatic journalistic exemption.

assumptions: Submissions usually arrive as documents, and substantive revisions are discussed with their authors.
The editor's assessment remains a required input to substantive rewriting.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Consent and access includes content-processing permission and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Document formats and support for reliable tracked changes.
Manuscript confidentiality, personal data and permitted processing environments.
Quality and availability of source packs and style rules.
Acceptance authority and demand from first-time contributors.
research_questions: Which proposed edits alter meaning despite passing style checks?
Does revision comparison reliably preserve comments, quotations and formatting?
Which author groups benefit from guided briefs before submitting a manuscript?
new_work: Review tracked revisions and verify factual changes.
Maintain term lists, house-style rules and documented exceptions.
Handle failed comparisons and conflicting document versions.
Check processing permissions and remove expired manuscript copies.
Support first-time authors with briefs and feedback.

tasks.short: Select relevant newswire items for the publication's audience and editorial purpose.

steps.what: Browse incoming local, national and international items in the newswire reader.
Check candidate items against duplicates, updates and previously used coverage.
Read remaining items and compare their relevance, novelty and audience interest.

loop.input: Licensed newswire text, audience brief, editorial criteria and current content plan.
loop.output: Suggested topic labels and shortlist with source-linked reasons and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Validate item identifiers and quoted passages; retain the full screened list for editor inspection.
loop.stop: One classification pass per item and one repair for invalid output; failures remain visible as unclassified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata filters cover location and topics, but contextual relevance needs reading the text.

steps.what: Choose items based on significance, balance, timeliness and potential audience impact.
Record selected items and send source references to the assigned writer.

tasks.design: A deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} imports licensed newswire items from the {OTHER}, a newswire reader, and groups duplicates and updates using identifiers and text fingerprints. A bounded classifier feeds a review view in the {BI}; the editor's selection creates source-linked briefs in the {CMS} and {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feed readers provided search and alerts, but audience relevance and editorial balance required reading across many items.
tasks.enabler_now: Feed integration, deterministic filtering and bounded text classification can reduce scanning without automating editorial selection.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle developments, unfamiliar topics and minority interests can be missed by relevance filters. Licensing may restrict storage and model processing.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising significance beyond familiar keywords and balancing audience interest with coverage obligations.

ambition.what: A midday coverage-gap review of newly developing stories.

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time scanning repeated items and more time comparing significant developments and overlooked subjects. Selection authority remains unchanged.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Turn recurring news developments into audience and market questions.
reach.learn: Source triangulation, sampling bias and the difference between news volume and market importance.

reach.task: Develop a selected news item into an original audience-focused article.
reach.learn: Angle development, additional reporting and source attribution.

evidence.claim: Coosto provides news and conversation monitoring, supporting monitoring feasibility rather than autonomous editorial selection.
Mediahuis trials show editorial automation pipelines exist, with a person publishing; they do not establish a need for an agent here.
Feed identifiers, update links, timestamps and exact-text fingerprints support deterministic screening.
EU AI Act transparency requirements need assessment if downstream publication includes generated public-interest text.

assumptions: This marketing editor works on a publication that uses a licensed trade or general newswire.
Screening groups exact duplicates and linked updates; uncertain similarities remain visible.
Selection creates an internal brief and does not itself publish material.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Consent and access includes feed licensing, processing permissions and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether a newswire subscription exists and provides usable integration access.
Feed licensing terms for storage, classification and republication.
Audience priorities, coverage obligations and current selection criteria.
Availability of stable item identifiers and update relationships.
research_questions: Which important items would the proposed shortlist omit?
Do duplicate groups ever conceal a material update?
Does the shortlist overrepresent familiar subjects or high-volume sources?
Can a midday review fit production deadlines and editorial capacity?
new_work: Sample items outside the shortlist to detect systematic omissions.
Review uncertain classifications and incorrectly grouped updates.
Maintain topic criteria, feed mappings and licensing controls.
Monitor feed failures and retain a usable manual reading route.

role.altitude: The editor's week shifts from source hunting, repeated copy handling and plan assembly toward editorial judgement, author development and audience understanding. Publishing and acceptance rights remain with their existing holders; any wider commissioning or scheduling authority needs explicit delegation.
reach: Public Relations Specialists: explain recurring public concerns and manage escalations.
Marketing Managers: connect editorial priorities to audience needs and production capacity.
Technical Writers: help subject-matter authors communicate accurately.
Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists: investigate coverage gaps and emerging audience questions.
skills_to_grow: Translate editorial policy into testable rules while documenting exceptions.
Review source-linked drafts and detect changes in meaning.
Evaluate retrieval omissions and shortlist bias.
Maintain permissions, content rights and version provenance.
Coach contributors and facilitate difficult editorial conversations.
role.ambitious_version: Run an audience-led editorial service with a reader-question digest, a supported route for first-time contributors and frequent coverage-gap reviews. Use the recovered preparation time to commission clearer, better-supported material within a delegated editorial remit.
